'''Carlos Manuel Duarte''' is a [[marine ecologist]] conducting research on [[marine ecosystem]]s globally, from polar to the tropical ocean and from near-shore to deep-sea ecosystems. His research addresses biodiversity in the oceans, the impacts of human activity on marine ecosystems, and the capacity of marine ecosystems to recover from these impacts. He is also interested in transdisciplinary research, collaborating with scientists and engineers across a broad range of fields to solve problems in the marine ecosystem and society. He is currently a Distinguished Professor at the [[King Abdullah University of Science and Technology]] and executive director of the Coral Research and Development Accelerator Platform.<ref>{{cite web | title=CORDAP |date=22 March 2022 |url=https://cordap.org/members/}}</ref><ref name="KAUSTProfile">{{cite web |title=Carlos M. Duarte – Faculty Profile |url=https://www.kaust.edu.sa/en/study/faculty/carlos-duarte |website=King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) |access-date=14 October 2025}}</ref>

==Education==
Duarte earned a bachelor's degree in [[environmental biology]] from [[Autonomous University of Madrid]], Spain, in 1982. In 1987, he obtained a Ph.D. in [[limnology]] from [[McGill University]], advised by Jacob Kalff.<ref name="McGill">{{cite web |title=Carlos Duarte – Alumni Profile |url=https://www.mcgill.ca/biology |publisher=McGill University |access-date=14 October 2025}}</ref><ref name="SeaLegacy">{{cite web |title=Carlos Duarte – Scientist |url=https://sealegacy.org/community/carlos-duarte/ |publisher=SeaLegacy |access-date=14 October 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
Upon receiving a Ph.D. in biology, Duarte returned to Spain where he was a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the Instituto de Ciencias del Mar (1987–1989), to then take a position as staff researcher with the [[Spanish National Research Council]] therein, and move to the ranks to research professor while moving to the Blanes Centre for Advanced Studies (1989–1999), and to the Mediterranean Institute for Advanced Studies, Mallorca (1999–2015). In 2011 Duarte took the role of inaugural director, and Winthrop Professor, at the UWA Oceans Institute, [[University of Western Australia]]. In 2015 he joined the Biological and Environmental Science and Engineering Division and the Red Sea Research Center at [[King Abdullah University of Science and Technology]], where he was appointed director of the Red Sea Research Center from 2016 to 2018. He also joined the Computational Biology Research Center there in 2017.<ref name="KAUSTProfile" />
He is the founding editor-in-chief of ''Frontiers in Marine Science'',<ref>{{Cite journal|doi=10.3389/fmars.2018.00337|title=Ocean Solutions to Address Climate Change and Its Effects on Marine Ecosystems|year=2018|last1=Gattuso|first1=Jean-Pierre|last2=Magnan|first2=Alexandre K.|last3=Bopp|first3=Laurent|last4=Cheung|first4=William W. L.|last5=Duarte|first5=Carlos M.|last6=Hinkel|first6=Jochen|last7=McLeod|first7=Elizabeth|last8=Micheli|first8=Fiorenza|last9=Oschlies|first9=Andreas|last10=Williamson|first10=Phillip|last11=Billé|first11=Raphaël|last12=Chalastani|first12=Vasiliki I.|last13=Gates|first13=Ruth D.|last14=Irisson|first14=Jean-Olivier|last15=Middelburg|first15=Jack J.|last16=Pörtner|first16=Hans-Otto|last17=Rau|first17=Greg H.|journal=Frontiers in Marine Science|volume=5|page=337 |s2cid=52912765|doi-access=free|bibcode=2018FrMaS...5..337G |hdl=10754/629968|hdl-access=free}}</ref> and served or has served in the editorial board of multiple scientific journals. He has published over 900 scientific papers and many books and book chapters and supervised a large number of students and early career researchers.<ref>{{cite web | title=Google Scholar |url=https://scholar.google.es/citations?user=T2-L50AAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao/ }}</ref> He served as elected President of the American Society of Limnology and Oceanography, the largest professional society on marine sciences, and has received multiple awards and honors for his research contributions.

He has been recognized as a "Highly Cited Researcher", demonstrated by the production of multiple highly cited papers that rank in the top 1% by citations for a research field, in all the assessments conducted thus far, including the 2018 assessment,<ref>{{cite web | title=Highly cited researchers |url= https://hcr.clarivate.com// }}</ref> and in 2019 was ranked within the top 0.01% (ranked 887 among 7 million scientists evaluated) across all fields, the top ranked scientists in Marine Biology and Hydrology.<ref>{{cite web | title= KAUST continues notable presence in Highly Cited Researchers list|url= https://www.kaust.edu.sa/en/news/kaust-continues-notable-presence-in-highly-cited-researchers-list}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Baas |first1=Jeroen |title=Supplementary data tables for "A standardized citation metrics author database annotated for scientific field" (PLoS Biology 2019) |last2=Ionnadis |first2=John P. A. |last3=Klavans |first3=Richard |last4=Boyack |first4=Kevin |publisher=Mendeley |year=2019 |volume=1 |chapter=Bibliometrics |doi=10.17632/btchxktzyw.1 |chapter-url=https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/btchxktzyw/1}}</ref> In 2021 Duarte was ranked, by [[Reuters]], as the 12th most influential climate scientist in the world.<ref>{{cite news | title= The Reuters Hot List: World's top climate scientists|newspaper= Reuters|url= https://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/climate-change-scientists-list/}}</ref> He was also ranked the 4th top scientist in [[Ecology and Evolution]], and the top marine scientist in their rank.<ref>{{cite web | title= Top Ecology and Evolution Scientists|url= https://research.com/scientists-rankings/ecology-and-evolution}}</ref> Since 2021 Duarte also serves as executive director for the Global Coral R&D Accelerator Platform, CORDAP. On October 27, 2021, Prof. Duarte has been appointed Academic with the [[Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences]] for his seminal contributions to further understanding marine ecosystems and their responses to [[global change]].<ref>{{cite web |date=27 October 2021 |title=Duarte appointed Academic with Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences |url=https://rsrc.kaust.edu.sa/news/detail/2021/11/02/distinguished-professor-carlos-m.-duarte-has-been-appointed-academic-with-the-spanish-royal-academy-of-sciences |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211102064326/https://rsrc.kaust.edu.sa/news/detail/2021/11/02/distinguished-professor-carlos-m.-duarte-has-been-appointed-academic-with-the-spanish-royal-academy-of-sciences |archive-date=2 November 2021 |access-date=21 December 2022 |website=Red Sea Research Center}}</ref>

==Research==
Duarte was originally trained as a limnologist and has contributed to understanding the ecology of freshwater plants in rivers and lakes, as well as the role of freshwater ecosystems in carbon cycling. His research in the ecology and [[biogeochemistry]] of [[seagrass meadow]]s and other vegetated coastal systems eventually lead – in collaboration with different UN agencies - to the development of "Blue carbon" strategies to [[Climate change mitigation|mitigate climate change]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Nellemann |first1=Christian |last2=Corcoran |first2=Emily |last3=Duarte |first3=Carlos |last4=Valdes |first4=Luis |last5=De Young |first5=Cassandra |last6=Fonseca |first6=Luciano |last7=Grimsditch |first7=Gabriel |date=2009 |title= Blue Carbon. The role of healthy oceans in binding carbon. A Rapid Response Assessment, United Nations Environment Programme, GRID-Arendal.|url=https://ccom.unh.edu/sites/default/files/publications/Nellemann_2010_BlueCarbon_book.pdf |location=Norway |page=80 |isbn= 978-82-7701-060-1}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Duarte |first1=Carlos |last2=Cebrián |first2=Just |date= December 1996 |title=The fate of marine autotrophic production |journal=Limnology and Oceanography |volume=41 |issue=8 |pages=1758–1766 |doi=10.4319/lo.1996.41.8.1758 |bibcode=1996LimOc..41.1758D |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1= C. M. Duarte |last2=J.J. Middelburg |last3=N. Caraco |date= 2005 |title=Major role of marine vegetation on the oceanic carbon cycle |journal=Biogeosciences |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=1–8|doi=10.5194/bg-2-1-2005 |bibcode=2005BGeo....2....1D |doi-access=free |hdl=10261/88911 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
Recognizing the many gaps in our understanding of the deep-sea pelagic ecosystem, Duarte led the Malaspina Circumnavigation Expedition, involving more than 500 scientists, and that sailed the oceans between 2010 and 2011 to provide a global assessment of the deep-sea pelagic ecosystem. The [[Malaspina Expedition 2010]] has thus far released over 200 publications addressing different aspects of the biodiversity and function of the deep-sea ecosystem.<ref>{{cite journal |last=C.M.
